subject: Sundial Retail - AZ2 latency/error bleed; request for cross-region canary and exec attention
messages:
From: Alex Novak <alex.novak@sundialretail.com>
To: grace_oconnor@redwood.ai
Cc: ops@sundialretail.com
Date: 2028-03-15T08:12:00-07:00
Subject: Sudden latency + 5xx spike for Sundial - visible across checkout region (AZ2)

Grace —

We are seeing a sharp degradation impacting checkout traffic routed to AZ2 (us-east-2). Starting ~07:55 PT our telemetry shows: p95 latency rose from ~220ms to ~2.3s, 5xx error rate ~8% (from baseline 0.3%), and overall throughput is down ~35% compared to the last hour. This is hitting peak shopping traffic now.

Attached: sundial_kpi_sla.pdf (SLA thresholds) and a short network dump (network-trace-0315.log). Ops pager alerted us and we've throttled non-critical feature flags, but conversions are dropping fast.

Can Redwood perform an emergency cross-region canary (us-west-2) or drain AZ2 while preserving session affinity? We need an exec loop if this requires priority capacity or credits. Please advise immediate next steps and ETA.

— Alex Novak
Head of Infrastructure, Sundial Retail
From: grace_oconnor@redwood.ai
To: Alex Novak <alex.novak@sundialretail.com>
Cc: david_kim@redwood.ai, hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-03-15T08:19:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Sudden latency + 5xx spike for Sundial - visible across checkout region (AZ2)

Alex — thanks for the alert and the artifacts. I'm escalating internally and will coordinate the immediate mitigation. High-level plan:

- Triage + confirm root indicators (David).
- Prepare controlled cross-region canary to us-west-2 (Hannah/routing).
- If canary is successful, perform phased drain of AZ2 for Sundial's traffic and failover to us-west-2.
- Notify you at each step; keep a rollback window.

Can you confirm if any customer sessions require sticky KV state that cannot be reconstructed if routed to a different region? If so, we will route only new sessions and preserve old sessions to AZ2 for 10 minutes.

I've CC'd David and Hannah — we'll post an ops link and a single comms thread for updates.

— Grace O'Connor
Senior AM, Redwood Inference
From: david_kim@redwood.ai
To: grace_oconnor@redwood.ai
Cc: hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai, alex.novak@sundialretail.com
Date: 2028-03-15T09:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Sudden latency + 5xx spike for Sundial - visible across checkout region (AZ2)

On Wed, Mar 15, 2028 at 08:19 Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Alex — thanks for the alert and the artifacts. I'm escalating internally and will coordinate the immediate mitigation.

Quick triage summary (initial):
- Telemetry aligns with cache eviction/KV cache saturation around 07:50 PT in us-east-2. KV hit ratio for the affected model dropped from 87% to ~42%.
- Several inference hosts in AZ2 are reporting elevated kernel queue times and repeated model load retries (GPU OOMs not evident but high memory pressure).
- Error signature: the majority of 5xx traces are internal load-balancer timeouts and retry amplification on long-tail requests.

Proposed mitigation (technical):
1) Spin up a small dedicated warm pool in us-west-2 with the same model variant (quantized) — 10 nodes can absorb ~40% of peak for Sundial's traffic per our estimate. (ETA: 14–18 min).
2) Run a 5-minute canary at 5% of live traffic to us-west-2 (session-aware: new sessions only) to validate latency/5xx behavior.
3) If canary passes (p95 < 350ms and 5xx < 1%), progressively move up to 50% over 20 minutes, then full shift if stable.
4) If canary fails, failback and prepare a temporary model fallback (lighter decoder config) to reduce memory/KV pressure.

I attached a short network trace excerpt and I'll push more logs to the shared drive. We'll also enable detailed token-level tracing for affected requests.

I'll coordinate capacity with infra and throttling with routing. Grace, please open the ops incident link for live updates.

— David Kim
Principal Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai
To: grace_oconnor@redwood.ai, david_kim@redwood.ai
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, alex.novak@sundialretail.com
Date: 2028-03-15T09:28:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Sudden latency + 5xx spike for Sundial - visible across checkout region (AZ2)

Team — quick routing note and ask for exec approval:

Planned canary steps (routing ops):
- Implement canary by setting a route rule: Sundial checkout -> 5% to us-west-2 (new sessions only); 95% remaining to AZ2.
- Monitor latencies and 5xx at 1-minute granularity in the first 10 minutes.
- If metrics are green, scale to 25% (10 min), then 50% (20 min).
- Full drain plan requires coordination for reserved capacity bump or temporary burst and potential SLA credit sign-off.

Ask for:
- Marissa (Sales) — please approve emergency priority for reserved capacity if we need to exceed normal quotas.
- Exec/leadership — visible approval for the routing shift so we can trigger the reserved warm pool and make a go/no-go decision quickly.

If approved I will initiate the canary immediately and post live metrics to the incident link.

— Hannah Schmitt
Routing & Capacity, Redwood Inference
From: Alex Novak <alex.novak@sundialretail.com>
To: grace_oconnor@redwood.ai
Cc: hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai, david_kim@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-03-15T16:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Sudden latency + 5xx spike for Sundial - visible across checkout region (AZ2)

Grace/Hannah/David —

Thanks for the rapid triage and proposed plan. We approve the canary and subsequent progressive cutover to us-west-2. We don't have sticky session state that would block new-session routing; preserving existing checkout sessions in AZ2 for 10 minutes is fine.

Please notify our ops pager when the 5% canary is live and again at 25% and 50%. We will expect a postmortem and confirmation on any SLA credit eligibility once the incident is closed.

— Alex Novak
Head of Infrastructure, Sundial Retail
